Simmer the chicken with the onion and water for 30 minutes, skimming the foam, then lift out, shred and keep the broth.
Fry the vermicelli in 1 tbsp oil until golden, add the rinsed rice and 600 ml broth, cover and cook on low for 18 minutes.
Fry the garlic and fresh coriander in the remaining oil with the ground coriander for 1 minute until fragrant.
Bring 800 ml broth to a simmer, add the mloukhiyeh and half the garlic mixture, and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes without boiling hard.
Stir in the shredded chicken, the rest of the garlic mixture and salt, and serve over the rice with lemon juice.
Pat the tofu dry and fry the cubes in 2 tbsp oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Beat the eggs with spring onion and a pinch of salt, stir in the tofu, and pour into the pan with the rest of the oil.
Cook on medium for 3 minutes until set underneath, flip carefully and cook 2 minutes more.
Pound the garlic and chilli, then mix with kecap manis, lime juice and 2 tbsp warm water to make the sauce.
Top the omelette with bean sprouts, drizzle with the sauce and finish with peanuts and fried shallots.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies, turmeric and lemongrass to a smooth paste.
Mash the tofu and mix with the paste, mushrooms, basil, lime leaves, egg and salt.
Spoon the mixture onto the banana leaves, fold into parcels and secure with toothpicks.
Steam the parcels for 15 minutes to set the filling.
Grill or dry-fry the parcels for 5 minutes until the leaves char, then serve warm with rice.
Fry the potato cubes in 3 tbsp oil until golden and cooked through, then drain.
Boil the beef cubes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and briefly blanch the liver for 3 minutes, then drain both.
Blend the chillies, shallots and garlic and fry the paste in the remaining oil with galangal and bay leaves for 5 minutes.
Add the beef, liver, coconut milk, palm sugar and salt and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Fold in the potatoes, cook 2 minutes more and serve with rice.
Simmer the beef in the water for 45 minutes until tender, skimming the surface.
Blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts and coriander and fry the paste in the ghee with lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes.
Add the paste to the beef with the coconut milk and milk and simmer gently for 10 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and stir in the fried potatoes.
Serve in bowls with tomato wedges and fried shallots, with rice on the side.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes, drain and snip into shorter lengths.
Fry the garlic and shallots in the oil until fragrant, then add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs, then add the carrot and cabbage and cook 2 minutes.
Add the noodles with both soy sauces and white pepper and toss for 3 minutes until evenly coated.
Finish with spring onion and serve hot.
Simmer the beef in the water with lemongrass, cinnamon and star anise for 50 minutes, then lift out the beef and keep the broth.
Slice the beef thinly and fry in 3 tbsp oil until crisp, then drain.
Blend the shallots, garlic and ginger, fry the paste in the remaining oil for 4 minutes and stir it into the broth with salt.
Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 5 minutes and drain.
Serve the noodles and halved eggs in bowls, ladle over the hot broth and top with crispy beef and spring onion.
Simmer the beef in the water for 45 minutes until tender, skimming as it cooks.
Blend the shallots, garlic, turmeric, ginger and candlenuts and fry the paste in the oil with lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes.
Stir the paste into the soup, season with salt and simmer 10 minutes more.
Blanch the bean sprouts for 30 seconds.
Serve the soup over the bean sprouts with halved eggs, fried shallots and lime wedges.
Blend the shallots, garlic, coriander and galangal to a paste.
Simmer the whole beef with the paste, coconut water, bay leaves, palm sugar, tamarind and salt for 40 minutes until tender and the liquid has reduced.
Cool slightly, slice the beef 1 cm thick along the grain and gently pound each slice to flatten.
Fry the slices in hot oil for 2 minutes per side until caramelised and golden.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies, ginger, turmeric and coriander to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil with star anise, cardamom, cinnamon and lemongrass for 6 minutes until fragrant.
Add the lamb and stir for 5 minutes to coat and seal.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the coconut milk and salt and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, then serve with rice.
Boil the sweet potato in the water for 12 minutes until soft, then blend to a smooth broth.
Blend the shallots, garlic and dried shrimp and fry in the oil with coriander and tomato paste for 4 minutes.
Add the sweet potato broth, bring to a simmer and add the prawns for 3 minutes, seasoning with salt.
Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts in boiling water for 1 minute and divide into bowls.
Ladle over the thick broth with prawns and top with halved eggs and lime wedges.
Wash the water spinach well and separate the stems from the leaves.
Fry the garlic, shallots and chillies in the oil over high heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the stems first and stir-fry for 1 minute, then add the leaves.
Add the soy sauce, sugar and water and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted.
Season with salt and serve immediately with rice.
Blanch the spinach, bean sprouts, long beans and cabbage separately in boiling water for 1 to 3 minutes each and drain.
Pound or blend the peanuts with garlic, chillies, lime leaves, palm sugar, tamarind and salt to a coarse paste.
Loosen the paste with the warm water to a thick pouring sauce.
Arrange the vegetables and cucumber on plates.
Spoon the peanut sauce over and serve with rice or rice cakes.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies and turmeric to a paste and mix with lemongrass, lime juice and salt.
Cut the fish into portions and coat well with the paste.
Lay each portion on a banana leaf with basil, lime leaves and tomato slices, fold into parcels and secure.
Grill them for 5 minutes until the leaves are charred and serve with rice.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies and coriander to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil with galangal and bay leaves for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the water, carrot and chayote and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the long beans, eggplant and coconut milk and simmer gently for 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the fried tofu, season with salt and serve with rice.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic and tomatoes to a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the oil with lime leaves for 8 minutes until darker and the oil separates.
Add the palm sugar, tamarind, water and salt and stir well.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until pink and coated.
Rub the chicken with lime juice and salt and set aside for 10 minutes.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic and ginger to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil with lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, tomatoes and water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until cooked and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the basil, check the salt and serve with rice.
Blend all the spices, shallots, garlic, chillies, candlenuts and lemongrass with the oil and salt to a paste, then fry it for 5 minutes.
Rub the duck inside and out with the paste and stuff the cavity with the lime leaves and some paste.
Wrap the duck tightly in banana leaves and then foil.
Roast at 160°C for 2 hours until very tender.
Unwrap, spoon over the juices and serve with rice and vegetables.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies and galangal; fry two-thirds of the paste in 2 tbsp oil with lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes.
Add the beef and coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 40 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and dark like rendang.
Fry the remaining paste in 1 tbsp oil with palm sugar, add the peeled eggs and roll to coat for sambal eggs.
Stir-fry the long beans in the last oil with salt for 4 minutes and cook the rice.
Serve the rice with the beef, sambal eggs and long beans arranged around it.
Blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts and coriander to a paste.
Simmer the chicken with the paste, coconut water, galangal, bay leaves, palm sugar, kecap manis and salt for 25 minutes until the liquid is almost gone.
Let the chicken cool and dry slightly.
Fry the pieces in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden.
Serve with rice, sambal and fresh cucumber.
Mix both minces with onion, garlic, mint, oregano, breadcrumbs, egg, salt and pepper and shape into small balls.
Fry the meatballs in 3 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Cook the rice in 500 ml salted water with the remaining oil for 15 minutes, covered.
Stir the lemon zest, juice and dill through the rice.
Serve the meatballs over the lemon rice with extra lemon wedges.
Brown the beef with onion and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, add tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, salt and pepper and simmer for 15 minutes.
Boil the pasta for 2 minutes less than the packet time and drain.
Whisk the yogurt with eggs and half the parmesan.
Layer pasta and meat sauce in a baking dish, spread the yogurt topping over and sprinkle with the rest of the parmesan.
Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until golden, rest 5 minutes and serve in bowls.
Marinate the chicken in 2 tbsp oil, lemon juice, half the garlic, oregano and salt for at least 15 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill for 12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Mix the yogurt with the cucumber, remaining garlic and salt to make tzatziki.
Chop the tomatoes and onion, toss with olives, the remaining oil and top with feta for the salad.
Warm the pitas and serve with the skewers, tzatziki and salad.
Toss the potato wedges with 2 tbsp oil, oregano, salt and lemon juice and roast at 200°C for 35 minutes.
Mix the beef with onion, garlic, mint, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper.
Divide into 6, wrap each portion around a piece of feta and flatten into patties.
Brush with the remaining oil and grill or pan-fry for 5 to 6 minutes per side.
Brown the beef in the oil, add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, cinnamon, bay leaves, allspice, salt and 500 ml water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Transfer to a baking dish, stir in the orzo and the remaining hot water.
Bake at 180°C for 25 minutes, stirring once, until the orzo is tender and has absorbed the sauce.
Serve topped with the grated cheese.
Simmer the chicken with onion, carrot, celery and salt in the water for 20 minutes, then lift out the chicken and shred it.
Strain the broth, bring back to a simmer and cook the rice in it for 15 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice until frothy.
Slowly whisk two ladles of hot broth into the egg mixture, then stir it back into the pot off the heat until silky.
Add the chicken, season with pepper and serve with dill.
Toss all the vegetables and garlic with the olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper in a large roasting dish.
Add 100 ml water, cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes.
Uncover, stir gently and roast 25 minutes more until golden and soft.
Scatter with parsley and crumbled feta and serve with bread.
Marinate the lamb with oil, half the garlic, oregano, paprika, cumin, lemon juice and salt for 15 minutes.
Fry the lamb in a very hot pan in batches for 3 minutes until charred at the edges.
Mix the yogurt, cucumber, remaining garlic and salt to make tzatziki.
Warm the pitas in a dry pan.
Fill with lamb, tomato, onion, lettuce and tzatziki, then roll up and serve.
Marinate the beef in oil, lemon juice, two crushed garlic cloves, oregano, salt and pepper for 20 minutes.
Cook the rice in 500 ml salted water for 15 minutes, covered.
Mix the yogurt, cucumber, last garlic clove and salt for tzatziki.
Thread the beef onto skewers and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning.
Serve with the rice, warm pitas, tzatziki and sliced tomato and onion.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, mustard, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss the chicken, potatoes and garlic in the dressing and spread in a large roasting tin with the water.
Roast for 45 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway, until the chicken is golden and the potatoes have soaked up the juices.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with the pan juices.
Brush the eggplant slices with 3 tbsp oil and roast at 200°C for 20 minutes until soft and golden.
Brown the beef with onion and garlic in the last oil, add tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt, eggs, nutmeg and half the parmesan.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in a dish, top with the yogurt mixture and remaining parmesan.
Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until set and golden, then spoon into bowls.
Cook the onions, garlic, carrot and celery in the oil for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, honey, salt and 150 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the beans and dill and pour into a baking dish.
Bake at 180°C for 35 minutes until the sauce is thick and the top is slightly crisp.
Serve warm with crumbled feta and bread.
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers, scoop out the tomato flesh and blend it with the sugar.
Soften the onion and garlic in half the oil, add the rice, pine nuts, half the tomato pulp, herbs, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Fill the vegetables three-quarters full, replace the tops and stand them in a dish with the potato wedges.
Pour over the remaining tomato pulp and oil with 150 ml water.
Bake at 190°C for 50 minutes until the rice is tender and the vegetables are blistered.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano and salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a baking dish, stir in the orzo and hot stock.
Bake at 190°C for 25 minutes, stirring once, until the orzo is tender.
Finish with lemon zest, parsley and grated cheese.
Soften the onion and spring onions in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the spinach a handful at a time until wilted.
Pour in the hot water with salt and pepper, cover and simmer for 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir in the dill and lemon juice and rest 5 minutes.
Brown the beef in the oil in batches, then return it all to the pot.
Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then the vinegar, tomatoes, spices, salt, pepper and 300 ml water.
Add the pearl onions and simmer 30 minutes more until the beef is tender and the sauce is glossy.
Cook the rice and serve the stifado over it.
Rub the lamb with oil, lemon juice, oregano, crushed garlic, salt and pepper and leave for 15 minutes.
Lay two large sheets of baking paper in a deep dish and pile in the potatoes, onion, tomatoes and remaining garlic.
Put the lamb on top with rosemary and cheese, pour over any marinade and seal the paper tightly, then cover with foil.
Roast at 160°C for 2 hours until the lamb falls off the bone.
Open the parcel, roast 15 minutes more to colour and serve with the juices.
Marinate the chicken in oil, lemon juice, oregano, half the garlic and salt for 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked.
Mix the yogurt, cucumber, remaining garlic and salt for tzatziki.
Fill with lettuce, tomato, onion, chicken and tzatziki and wrap tightly.
Marinate the chicken with 2 tbsp oil, the spices, oregano, one crushed garlic clove, lemon juice and salt for 20 minutes.
Toss the potatoes with the last oil and salt and bake at 220°C for 30 minutes until crisp.
Pan-fry or grill the chicken for 6 minutes per side, rest and slice thinly.
Mix yogurt, cucumber, the other garlic clove and salt for tzatziki, and toss tomato and onion with salt for the salad.
Serve the chicken with fries, warm pitas, tzatziki and salad.
Brush the fish with 2 tbsp oil, half the oregano, salt and pepper.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes per side until it flakes easily.
Toss the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, pepper and olives with the remaining oil and salt.
Top the salad with the feta in one piece and sprinkle with the last oregano.
Serve the fish with lemon wedges and the salad.
Marinate the paneer and pepper in yogurt with half the garam masala, the chilli powder, turmeric and salt for 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the paneer and pepper for 6 minutes until charred at the edges.
Fry the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic and ginger, then the tomatoes and remaining garam masala and simmer for 12 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth, return to the pan and stir in the cream and crushed fenugreek.
Add the paneer and peppers, simmer 3 minutes and serve with naan or rice.
Heat the oil and fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic and chilli for 1 minute, then the turmeric and ground coriander.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower with salt and toss to coat, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook uncovered for 8 minutes, stirring gently, until the vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle with garam masala and fresh coriander and serve.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, then the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then the ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Add the chickpeas, anardana, salt and 250 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Finish with fresh coriander and serve with rice or bread.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, add the onion and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli, then the mince, breaking it up, and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the ground spices and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the peas, salt and 100 ml water and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and serve with rice or roti.
Fry the onions in the ghee for 15 minutes until deep golden, remove half for the topping.
Add the lamb, garlic, ginger, yogurt, biryani masala, chilli, turmeric, half the herbs and salt and cook covered for 45 minutes until tender.
Boil the rice with cardamom, bay leaves and salt for 6 minutes until three-quarters cooked and drain.
Layer the rice over the lamb, scatter the remaining herbs and fried onions and drizzle the saffron milk.
Seal with a lid and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.
Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, cool in cold water and blend to a smooth purée.
Fry the paneer in 1 tbsp ghee until lightly golden and set aside.
Fry the cumin seeds in the remaining ghee, then the onion for 6 minutes, then garlic, ginger, chilli and tomato for 4 minutes.
Add the spinach purée, garam masala and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and paneer, heat through and serve with roti or rice.
Char the eggplants directly over a flame or under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning, until collapsed and smoky.
Cool, peel off the skin and mash the flesh.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, then the onion for 6 minutes, then garlic, ginger and chillies.
Add the tomatoes and ground spices and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the eggplant and salt, cook 5 minutes and finish with garam masala and fresh coriander.
Fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves in the oil until they pop, then the onion for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the ground spices, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tamarind and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk, simmer 5 minutes more and serve with rice.
Fry the whole spices in the oil for 1 minute, then the onions for 15 minutes until deep brown.
Add the garlic, ginger and chillies, then the beef, and fry over high heat for 10 minutes to sear.
Add the ground spices, tomatoes and salt and stir well.
Cover and cook on low for 50 minutes, adding a splash of water only if it sticks.
Uncover and fry (bhuna) for 10 minutes until the masala clings to the meat, then sprinkle with garam masala.
Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, half the herbs, half the fried onions and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Spread the marinated chicken in a heavy pot with 2 tbsp ghee.
Boil the rice with cardamom, cinnamon and salt for 6 minutes until 70% cooked and drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken with the remaining herbs, onions, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal the lid and cook on high for 5 minutes, then on very low for 40 minutes, rest 5 minutes and serve.
